newsitem.title: USA: Jitters dent Nasdaq for fourth session in a row.
newsitem.headline: Jitters dent Nasdaq for fourth session in a row.

text.p: Worries about the outlook for retail computer sales soaked tech stocks, sending the Nasdaq Composite Index south for the fourth consecutive session.

Traders said cautionary industry comments by a Salomon Brothers analyst sparked heavy selling. Concerns about the economy, the coming U.S. presidential election and tax-loss related selling added to the negative tone.
Salomon analyst David Childe said he expected worsening conditions for the computer industry, according to a source.
The Nasdaq Composite Index fell 12.83 to 1203.06 unofficially on volume of 564 million shares.
Market breadth was negative, with losing stocks beating gainers three to two.
Bellwether stock Intel Corp lost 1-5/8 to 104-3/8, Dell Computer lost 4-7/8 to 76-1/8, Sun Microsystems fell 7/8 to 58 and Microsoft fell 1-1/4 to 135-3/8.

DSP Communications shares fell 17-1/8 to 35-1/4 after the wireless chip maker agreed to buy Proxim Inc, which makes wireless communications gear and networking products. Proxim rose 2-51/64 to 21-1/2.
